# Single-flight readiness: admission before task creation

For asynchronous cache refresh, inspect where admission occurs: a try-lock acquired before task creation bounds checker tasks as well as upstream connections; acquiring it inside each spawned task would serialize upstream work while allowing an unbounded waiting-task queue. Startup and reload must use the same lock.

Price TTL expiry separately from event invalidations. A 600 s healthy TTL and 60 s failed TTL describe passive revalidation; refreshes, quota responses and explicit reloads can legitimately request earlier checks. Do not describe those TTLs as an unconditional upstream rate limit.

Retain separate scaling columns: a shared 30 s GET is constant request count, while existing seat decoding/splitting and health cloning/serialization remain fleet-sized. A Tokio task is not an OS process launch.

PR #243 reviewed head ed6462dbe3ce24e453ebeb47ad6ce8503721611d. CI run 44246537074, successful Rust job 134606837050, upload-selected artifact 14402062142: 2502 passed, 6 skipped; the eight focused regressions and six spawn-site witnesses passed. Author candidate receipts: 72 -> 72 launches over 60 s with five seats; three concurrent status reads during a stall started one readiness check.

Reviewer host observations are only a pre-feature baseline, not candidate deployment proof. The 20 s whole-machine sampler overlapped the 60 s CPU window; label observer overhead and attribution lower bounds explicitly.

**magicWand:** extend pr-freeze with a read-only review-proof receipt binding full head, CI conclusion, tested checkout, successful job and upload-selected artifact id, plus explicit local-gate exclusions.

**difficulties:** dispatch named a frozen head before checks finished; publication waited for FINAL. The dependency-free review worktree cannot produce a green local full harness gate without violating the no-build/no-dependency-repair packet; boot and quick-check failures were retained, and exact-head CI supplied build/test proof. Captured observations: COORD-001 and MW-001 in the pij-back-rooster buffer. Product and review trees remained unchanged.
